Subject: Embeddings storage gateway: partner feasibility and pilot scope

Hi all,

Following up from last week's partner sync — we want to validate a lightweight "embeddings storage gateway" pattern that gives customers a single vector API while tiering vectors between a hot vector DB (pgvector / Pinecone / Weaviate) and S3 cold storage. The goal: reduce Serving $/token and storage costs for long-tail vectors while keeping latency for recent queries.

Key asks for partners:
- Feasibility: can your product support a proxy or fallthrough routing model where a read first checks the hot index and then fetches from S3-backed persisted vectors (a reconstructed vector or pointer) for misses?
- Performance tradeoffs: measured read/write latency for cold reads reconstructed from S3, and any recommended batching or prefetch strategies.
- Security/ops: VPC peering options, request-level auth, and audit logs.
- Pilot scope: can you commit a small joint PoC (2 clients) over 6-8 weeks?

I've attached a short brief (gateway-poc-brief.pdf) that describes the interaction patterns and a suggested API shim. Internal recipients — Dev/Vanessa, please review constraints (networking, SOC2, and billing model) and flag anything blocking. External — can each partner respond with a short feasibility note + suggested pilot milestones by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: gateway-poc-brief.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@pinecone.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marta Silva <marta@weaviate.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@databridgelabs.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings storage gateway: partner feasibility and pilot scope

Thanks Aditya — this is interesting. Short answers up front: yes, Pinecone can act as the hot index and accept a proxy pattern. We typically see three options:

1) Pointer pattern: hot index stores key + minimal vector; misses return a pointer (S3 object key) so the application fetches and does a local similarity fallback.
2) Proxy-level reconstruction: a gateway fetches object(s) from S3, reconstructs embeddings (or loads stored embeddings) and returns a synthesized similarity result.
3) Hybrid prefetch: on write, we replicate small meta vectors to Pinecone and full vectors to S3; background workers backfill frequently-accessed vectors into Pinecone.

Performance notes: cold read (S3 fetch + vector deserialization + scoring) tends to be 120-400ms depending on object size and region+S3 GET latency; batching (fetch many keys in parallel) is crucial. We can supply a small test harness that simulates 1–2k QPS with fallthroughs to measure P99s.

Security/ops: we support VPC peering and private endpoints for our managed offering; audit logs are available via our enterprise tier. We can sign an NDA if you want to share example telemetry.

I'll attach a quick set of notes and a sample proxy sketch. Proposed pilot milestones: discovery + design (week 1), bench + harness (week 2–3), small customer PoC (weeks 4–8).

-Liam
Liam O'Connor
Partner Engineer, Pinecone

Attachment: pinecone-proxy-notes.md (text, 6KB)

Hi Aditya — we like the pattern and have implemented similar fallthrough flows for customers using our hybrid vector storage. A couple of items from Weaviate's side:

- We can store vector shards externally and stream them into the index for queries; our SDK supports async batch hydration from object stores.
- For security, we recommend signed presigned URLs for S3 GETs and a short-lived token exchange between the gateway and Weaviate to avoid long-lived credentials on the client.
- Weaviate can run as a private deployment inside a customer's VPC which simplifies network architecture for the pilot.

Notes for Redwood infra team (Dev/Vanessa): if you plan to do VPC peering into partner-managed services, we should scope egress rules and audit collection — happy to review the checklist.

Cheers,
Marta Silva
Head of Solutions, Weaviate

Subject: Re: Embeddings storage gateway: partner feasibility and pilot scope

Quick internal note — flagged items:

1) SOC2 / compliance: we cannot store customer-identifying metadata in cleartext on third-party buckets without DSAR and retention policies in place. We need partner confirmation on retention controls and purge APIs.
2) Network: VPC peering reduces egress but partners' managed offerings vary (some require NATed egress). We should plan for a TLS-based private link where possible.
3) Cost model: recommend we test both write-heavy and read-heavy workloads; partners should provide an estimate of per-miss unit cost (S3 GETs + reconstruction compute + partner query op).

I've attached a quick security constraints checklist (security-constraints-checklist.xlsx). Vanessa — can you confirm whether we prefer full VPC peering or a managed private endpoint for the pilot? Marissa — I want your input on which two pilot customers make sense (one high-query SaaS, one long-tail archiving customer).

-Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Platform

Aditya / team — DataBridge Labs is interested in participating as a pilot customer. A few items from procurement and product:

- Pilot goal: reduce long-term index storage cost by ~40% while preserving 95th%-ile recall for queries < 60 days.
- Success metrics: average P90 query latency, annualized storage $/embedding, and percent of queries served from hot index.
- Procurement: need a short MSA addendum for a limited PoC (term, data handling, liability caps). Deal id DB-1472.

Can partners provide a rough cost delta for a 6-week pilot and an initial runbook? We'll need a kickoff call next week.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Product, DataBridge Labs

- Pinecone will act as the hot index and provide a proxy harness for fallthrough testing. Weaviate will standby as an alternate hot index for a second customer if we want to compare behaviors.
- Security: partners to confirm retention/purge APIs and support for short-lived tokens or private endpoints.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Pinecone (Liam): deliver test harness and cost estimate for 6-week PoC by Tue, Apr 28.
- Weaviate (Marta): provide VPC/private-deployment checklist and token-exchange recommendations by Tue, Apr 28.
- Redwood (Dev): finalize security checklist and preferred network topology (VPC peering vs private endpoint) by Thu, Apr 29.
- Redwood (Marissa): confirm two pilot customers (DataBridge + fallback) and prep commercial addendum with Legal by Thu, Apr 29.
- Everyone: schedule a 30m kickoff for May 3 — proposed window 09:00–11:00 PT. Please add availability to the Calendly link: https://calendly.com/aditya-redwood/gateway-sync-30m

I'll prepare a one-pager for Legal/PS with the scope and success metrics. If partners can send cost numbers and the harness by Apr 28 we can lock in the kickoff.
